voci.titolo: Asian Stocks to Fall as Oil Stokes Inflation Fears: Markets Wrap
voci.riassunto: Asian stocks were poised to decline Thursday, tracking losses on Wall Street as surging oil prices and Treasury yields stoked inflation concerns ahead of key US price data. US oil extended its rally to an eighth straight session.

voci.titolo: Fund Veteran Says Australia Private Credit Should Be Less Opaque
voci.riassunto: Challenger Ltd., an Australian public and private credit markets investment manager, has thrown its support behind more disclosure for an industry facing heightened regulatory focus in the wake of Sydney property developer Bathla Group’s collapse.

voci.titolo: Oil’s surge back above $100 fuels fresh inflation fears at a crucial time for interest rates
voci.riassunto: A prolonged oil shock could keep consumer prices elevated and complicate the path for central banks already navigating a difficult policy environment.

voci.titolo: Bond Market Rate Spiral Has Potent Accelerator Behind the Scenes
voci.riassunto: The rush by bond investors to protect themselves against surging US yields risks exacerbating the spike, with behind-the-scenes hedging activity amplifying price swings.

voci.titolo: Husband & Wife Explore Sale of $37B Credit Firm
voci.riassunto: Bloomberg's Matt Monks joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Deals." Palmer Square Capital Management is a $37 billion credit firm run by the husband-wife duo Chris and Angie Long. And the couple is exploring a sale of the business. Under their leadership, the firm has grown to become one of the biggest issuers of collaterali

voci.titolo: U.S. reveals import ban on slew of Canadian goods as trade war escalates
voci.riassunto: Import bans on motorbikes, alcohol and dairy products are due to come into effect on Sept. 29 as the rift between the countries deepens.

voci.titolo: Bessent’s Upsized Buybacks Get Hit by Bond Market Reality
voci.riassunto: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s unusual move to supersize his department’s debt buyback program stumbled on Wednesday, when an announcement on the size of the first enlarged operation proved insufficient to halt market declines.

voci.titolo: Why the Fed's interest rate call could come down to a few hundredths of a percentage point
voci.riassunto: As markets vacillate between which way they see policymakers leaning, all eyes will turn to economic reports measuring producer and consumer prices.

voci.titolo: Dollar Ends Day at Lowest Since February as Bessent Aids Yen
voci.riassunto: The dollar finished the day at its weakest level in about seven months as the yen rallied after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent challenged traders to test his resolve on supporting Japan’s currency.

voci.titolo: Canada's retaliatory tariffs worth CA$27.6 billion take effect as trade rift with U.S. deepens
voci.riassunto: Duties on Canadian imports of U.S. steel and aluminum products have doubled to 50% as a trade war between Washington and Ottawa intensifies.

voci.titolo: Japan's foreign reserves drop by a record $80 billion in August following yen intervention
voci.riassunto: Finance ministry data showed that Japan's official foreign reserves stand at $1.207 trillion, down from July's figure of $1.287 trillion.

voci.titolo: China's imports in August miss estimates as calls for rebalancing trade grow
voci.riassunto: China's exports and imports gathered momentum in August, as the world's second-largest economy faces mounting pressure to rebalance trade.

voci.titolo: From ‘mystery vacations’ to hostels, budget travelers get thrifty as prices rise
voci.riassunto: Despite rising prices and the travel industry focusing on the luxury segment, budget-minded vacationers are still finding ways to get away.

voci.titolo: Trump turns up the heat on Warsh as Fed rate hike looms
voci.riassunto: Ten days ahead of the next Federal Reserve meeting, the Trump administration looks to be in a full-court press to halt a rate hike in its tracks.

voci.titolo: Women accounted for almost all of job gains in August. Here's why
voci.riassunto: Women accounted for virtually all of August's payroll gains, the latest sign of their growing power in the labor market.

voci.titolo: U.S. payrolls rose 162,000 in August, much more than expected; unemployment rate at 4.1%
voci.riassunto: Nonfarm payrolls were expected to increase by 53,000 in August while the unemployment rate held at 4.1%, according to the Dow Jones consensus.

voci.titolo: The big business of personal protection: How private security became a $50 billion industry
voci.riassunto: Private security spending and guard employment have climbed as companies and communities respond to high-profile attacks, even as violent crime falls.

voci.titolo: The big August jobs report is due out Friday. Here's what to expect for what has been a jobless summer
voci.riassunto: August nonfarm payrolls are expected to rise by 53,000 as a subdued labor market keeps Fed attention focused on inflation.
